instruction: Mirror-Symmetric Completion `scene.blend` contains a single mesh object `HalfPart` that is only the +X half of an intended X-symmetric shape: every vertex satisfies x >= 0 and the YZ cut-plane face at x=0 is present so the half-mesh is itself closed-manifold. Before starting the work, the Blender executable is `/opt/blender/blender`; use it to open `scene.blend`. Produce the full shape by mirroring `HalfPart` across the YZ plane (x=0) and merging the two halves along the centerline seam, then save the result as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. Requirements: 1. `answer.blend` opens as a valid Blender file. 2. The scene contains exactly one mesh object, named `Part`; `HalfPart` is absent. 3. `Part.location == (0,0,0)` and its modifier stack is empty. 4. `Part`'s mesh is closed-manifold: 0 non-manifold edges, 0 loose vertices, 0 loose edges. 5. `Part` is X-symmetric about x=0 within tol 1e-4: for every vertex `v`, a vertex also exists at `(-v.co.x, v.co.y, v.co.z)` within that tol. 6. `Part`'s axis-aligned bbox along X is symmetric about 0: `abs(min_x + max_x) < 1e-4` with `max_x > 0`. 7. `Part`'s bbox extents along Y and Z each match `HalfPart`'s original bbox on those axes within 1e-4. 8. `Part`'s vertex count equals `2 * N_half - N_seam`, where `N_half` is the input vertex count of `HalfPart` and `N_seam` is the number of input verts with `x ~= 0` (no duplicate seam verts). 9. `Part`'s unsigned volume is approximately 2x the input `HalfPart`'s volume (within 5%). The final shape must be fully symmetric across the YZ plane with no duplicated verts on the centerline.
